builds.name: Blade of the Erdtree
builds.description:
Blade of the Erdtree is a devastating bleed-focused dual-wield build that shreds every boss in the game. Designed around high Arcane 55, Vigor 50, Dexterity 45, this build achieves a moderate difficulty level that rewards game knowledge and mechanical skill. The build fully utilizes DLC content, incorporating endgame weapons, spells, and talismans that significantly elevate its performance.

In PvE, Blade of the Erdtree handles every challenge with confidence. Boss fights become a dance of positioning and timing as you leverage the Scavenger's Curved Sword's unique properties. Regular enemies and area traversal feel smooth thanks to the balanced stat investment — you have enough damage to clear trash efficiently and enough Vigor to survive surprises. The build prioritizes sustainable damage output through its primary stat while maintaining the defensive stats needed to learn new boss patterns without frustration.

The core strength of Blade of the Erdtree is its versatility and damage potential when optimized. Key items like Scavenger's Curved Sword are acquired through mid-game progression or specific questlines, allowing the build to come online at a reasonable point. The primary weakness is occasional reliance on specific items or buffs — maintaining uptime requires attention. Players should practice the core combos regularly to build muscle memory.

Blade of the Erdtree is ideal for players who have completed at least one playthrough and want to explore a different approach to combat. It rewards game knowledge — knowing where key items are, which bosses to tackle in order, and how to optimize your route makes a significant difference. While the core build functions with basic items, reaching its full potential requires exploring optional areas, completing specific NPC questlines, and understanding soft cap breakpoints for efficient leveling.

phases.name: Early Game
steps: Prioritize leveling Vigor/Vitality to comfortable levels before investing heavily in damage stats — survival comes first in the early game, aim for 20 Vigor before focusing on Arcane.
Explore Limgrave, Weeping Peninsula, Stormhill thoroughly. Each cave, catacomb, and ruin contains valuable upgrade materials, spells, and consumables crucial for progression.
Talk to every NPC you encounter — many offer questlines that reward essential items like Scavenger's Curved Sword or key upgrade materials later. Never attack NPCs unless you know their drops.
Save Smithing Stones and upgrade materials for weapons you'll use long-term. Your starting Samurai weapon is adequate while you rush toward Scavenger's Curved Sword.
Purchase a backup weapon from a merchant — having a Strike weapon for crystal/skeleton enemies and a Thrust weapon for armored foes covers all resistances.
Master your weapon's moveset in early areas. Practice spacing on basic soldiers, roll timing against large enemies, and learn which attacks have poise/hyper armor.
Summon NPC phantoms for tough early bosses if needed. Many games hide summon signs near boss fogs — the game expects you to use them.
Collect every flask upgrade item — Golden Seeds, Estus Shards, Sacred Tears. Each upgrade provides more value than several stat points for survival.
Revisit merchants after major story progression — they often stock new items, spells, or unlimited upgrade materials after key milestones.
Rush toward your build's defining weapon early. Run past enemies if necessary — the sooner you get Scavenger's Curved Sword, the sooner your build comes online.
Kill every optional boss and mini-boss you encounter. They drop unique weapons, talismans, and valuable souls/runes for early leveling.
Buy basic spells (Glintstone Pebble equivalent) from early vendors. Even weak spells are excellent for clearing trash packs and pulling enemies from safe range.
Keep Endurance/Stamina at comfortable levels (15-20 early). An extra swing or roll often means the difference between winning and dying.
Experiment with Weapon Arts / Skills early. The Choose Samurai for starting Uchigatana and high Dex determines your early game approach.
Check the Whetblade / Infusion item availability. Changing weapon affinity early lets you scale with your primary damage stat from the start.

phases.name: Mid Game
steps: Reach your weapon's stat requirements to unlock its full potential. Arcane should be your primary focus, with secondary investment in supporting stats.
Complete NPC questlines tied to your build. Many reward Scavenger's Curved Sword, powerful talismans, or unique spells. Check in with quest givers after each major boss.
Farm upgrade materials from specific mid-game enemies. Caelid and Altus Plateau have excellent farming spots for Chunks and upgrade materials.
Consider respeccing if your stats are suboptimal. Most games offer respec items (Larval Tear, Soul Vessel) — use them to fine-tune your Arcane investment.
Equip talismans/rings that synergize with your damage type. Arcane-boosting talismans (Scorpion Charms, Clutch Rings, Firstborn Rings) provide significant multipliers.
Explore optional areas before pushing main story progression. Mt. Gelmir and Nokron contain vital mid-game pickups for your build.
Join a covenant aligned with your playstyle. Many offer rewards like spell slots, faster casting, or damage buffs at rank milestones.
Invest in Mind/FP or Attunement if your build uses skills or spells. Running out of FP mid-fight is a common and preventable cause of death.
Find the best catalyst/seal/staff for your build. Dragon Communion Seal and Prince of Death's Staff provide hybrid scaling.
Practice your core combat loop against mid-game enemies. Learn boss punish windows and optimal damage combos for your weapon class.
Collect respec items and keep them for emergencies. Having 2-3 respecs available lets you experiment with different stat distributions.
Target 35-40 Vigor/Vitality by mid-game. Weapon upgrade level contributes more to damage than raw stats at this stage — invest in survival first.
Maintain medium roll (under 70% equip load) at minimum. Fast roll (under 30%) is ideal for lighter builds. Defense and poise protect more than fashion.
Use consumables matching boss weaknesses. Altus Plateau bosses are particularly vulnerable to specific damage types — prepare accordingly.
Stockpile crafting materials. Resins, spell buffs, and consumables for your damage type provide 15-30% DPS increases that scale with your upgrades.

phases.areas: Mountaintops, Farum Azula, Realm of Shadow
phases.areasVi: Mountaintops, Farum Azula, Realm of Shadow
steps: Push Arcane to the soft cap for maximum damage scaling. The 80 soft cap provides the best returns for spell scaling weapons.
Max your primary weapon to the highest upgrade level. Every level at high stat investment provides significant AR increases — check for Somber/Regular upgrade paths.
Farm the best talismans/rings/gems from endgame areas. Mountaintops of the Giants and Crumbling Farum Azula contain S-tier upgrades that transform your build's power.
Complete the DLC content before the final boss. DLC areas contain some of the game's best weapons, talismans, and spells — including direct upgrades for Scavenger's Curved Sword.
Stack multiplicative damage bonuses. Arcane Scorpion Charm, Clutch Ring, or covenant rings combined with skill damage talismans provide exponential returns.
Use Terra Magicus / Steady Chant / Magic-boosting physick before boss doors. Buffing before entering maximizes your burst damage windows.
Learn endgame boss patterns through repetition. Miquella's Haligtree and Realm of Shadow bosses have complex mix-ups — patience during first attempts pays off.
Optimize flask allocation per boss. Hard-hitting bosses demand more healing flasks, while spell-heavy builds should prioritize FP flasks for sustained damage.
Customize your Physick/Wondrous Elixir for each fight. Arcane-boosting tears combined with damage-negation tears cover offense and defense simultaneously.
Carry backup weapons with different damage types. A Strike weapon, a Standard weapon, and an elemental option handle any resistance profile.
Upgrade a secondary weapon to +9/+24 minimum. Status-infused backup weapons (Bleed, Frost, Poison) or different movesets give options against resistant bosses.
Aim for poise breakpoints if your build supports it. 51+ poise in Elden Ring, 40+ in DS3, or max poise in DS1 lets you trade through enemy attacks.
Equip the strongest defensive talisman available. Dragoncrest Greatshield / Steel Protection +3 provides 20% physical damage reduction — a massive effective HP boost.
Test your build against optional superbosses before the final encounter. If you can handle the hardest optional boss, the final boss is manageable.
Record your damage numbers before and after optimization. Understanding the difference between 60% optimization and 95% optimization helps prioritize remaining upgrades.

tips: Jumping L1 attacks apply status effects twice per button press for insane bleed buildup — always jump attack when possible
Multi-hit talismans (Rotten Winged Sword Insignia, Millicent's Prosthesis, Claw Talisman) stack multiplicatively
Seppuku ash of war triggers Lord of Blood's Exultation and White Mask buffs simultaneously
Keep a spare Blood-infused weapon for bosses immune to Occult-scaling bleed

Stat soft caps in Elden Ring: Vigor 40/60, Endurance 50, Str/Dex 55, Int/Fth/Arc 50/80. Know these for efficient leveling of Blade of the Erdtree.
Jump attacks are king in Elden Ring — they deal massive stance damage and are safe against most attacks. Scavenger's Curved Sword users should abuse jumping R2s.
Spirit Ash summons can completely change a boss fight. Mimic Tear is the best general-purpose option for Blade of the Erdtree.
Always carry a Strike weapon for crystal enemies and a Pierce weapon for heavily armored foes — Scavenger's Curved Sword may not handle all resistances.
The Wondrous Physick can be customized for each boss. Swap tears based on the fight for maximum advantage with Blade of the Erdtree.
Guard counters (block + R2) are incredibly strong. They deal high stance damage and can break most enemies when using heavy weapons.
If you're struggling with a boss, try more Vigor, better talismans, or swapping to a different weapon. Blade of the Erdtree has flexibility in gear choices.

Explore Limgrave, Weeping Peninsula, Stormhill thoroughly. Each cave, catacomb, and ruin contains valuable upgrade materials, spells, and consumables crucial for progression.
Talk to every NPC you encounter — many offer questlines that reward essential items like Blasphemous Blade or key upgrade materials later. Never attack NPCs unless you know their drops.
Save Smithing Stones and upgrade materials for weapons you'll use long-term. Your starting Hero weapon is adequate while you rush toward Blasphemous Blade.
Purchase a backup weapon from a merchant — having a Strike weapon for crystal/skeleton enemies and a Thrust weapon for armored foes covers all resistances.
Master your weapon's moveset in early areas. Practice spacing on basic soldiers, roll timing against large enemies, and learn which attacks have poise/hyper armor.
Summon NPC phantoms for tough early bosses if needed. Many games hide summon signs near boss fogs — the game expects you to use them.
Collect every flask upgrade item — Golden Seeds, Estus Shards, Sacred Tears. Each upgrade provides more value than several stat points for survival.
Revisit merchants after major story progression — they often stock new items, spells, or unlimited upgrade materials after key milestones.
Rush toward your build's defining weapon early. Run past enemies if necessary — the sooner you get Blasphemous Blade, the sooner your build comes online.
Kill every optional boss and mini-boss you encounter. They drop unique weapons, talismans, and valuable souls/runes for early leveling.
Buy basic spells (Glintstone Pebble equivalent) from early vendors. Even weak spells are excellent for clearing trash packs and pulling enemies from safe range.
Keep Endurance/Stamina at comfortable levels (15-20 early). An extra swing or roll often means the difference between winning and dying.
Experiment with Weapon Arts / Skills early. The Choose Hero for high Strength and Faith determines your early game approach.
Check the Whetblade / Infusion item availability. Changing weapon affinity early lets you scale with your primary damage stat from the start.

phases.name: Mid Game
steps: Reach your weapon's stat requirements to unlock its full potential. Vigor should be your primary focus, with secondary investment in supporting stats.
Complete NPC questlines tied to your build. Many reward Blasphemous Blade, powerful talismans, or unique spells. Check in with quest givers after each major boss.
Farm upgrade materials from specific mid-game enemies. Caelid and Altus Plateau have excellent farming spots for Chunks and upgrade materials.
Consider respeccing if your stats are suboptimal. Most games offer respec items (Larval Tear, Soul Vessel) — use them to fine-tune your Vigor investment.
Equip talismans/rings that synergize with your damage type. Vigor-boosting talismans (Scorpion Charms, Clutch Rings, Firstborn Rings) provide significant multipliers.
Explore optional areas before pushing main story progression. Mt. Gelmir and Nokron contain vital mid-game pickups for your build.
Join a covenant aligned with your playstyle. Many offer rewards like spell slots, faster casting, or damage buffs at rank milestones.
Invest in Mind/FP or Attunement if your build uses skills or spells. Running out of FP mid-fight is a common and preventable cause of death.
Find the best catalyst/seal/staff for your build. Dragon Communion Seal and Prince of Death's Staff provide hybrid scaling.
Practice your core combat loop against mid-game enemies. Learn boss punish windows and optimal damage combos for your weapon class.
Collect respec items and keep them for emergencies. Having 2-3 respecs available lets you experiment with different stat distributions.
Target 35-40 Vigor/Vitality by mid-game. Weapon upgrade level contributes more to damage than raw stats at this stage — invest in survival first.
Maintain medium roll (under 70% equip load) at minimum. Fast roll (under 30%) is ideal for lighter builds. Defense and poise protect more than fashion.
Use consumables matching boss weaknesses. Altus Plateau bosses are particularly vulnerable to specific damage types — prepare accordingly.
Stockpile crafting materials. Resins, spell buffs, and consumables for your damage type provide 15-30% DPS increases that scale with your upgrades.

phases.name: Late Game + DLC
steps: Push Vigor to the soft cap for maximum damage scaling. 40 is the standard soft cap for survivability stats.
Max your primary weapon to the highest upgrade level. Every level at high stat investment provides significant AR increases — check for Somber/Regular upgrade paths.
Farm the best talismans/rings/gems from endgame areas. Mountaintops of the Giants and Crumbling Farum Azula contain S-tier upgrades that transform your build's power.
Complete the DLC content before the final boss. DLC areas contain some of the game's best weapons, talismans, and spells — including direct upgrades for Blasphemous Blade.
Stack multiplicative damage bonuses. Vigor Scorpion Charm, Clutch Ring, or covenant rings combined with skill damage talismans provide exponential returns.
Use Terra Magicus / Steady Chant / Magic-boosting physick before boss doors. Buffing before entering maximizes your burst damage windows.
Learn endgame boss patterns through repetition. Miquella's Haligtree and Realm of Shadow bosses have complex mix-ups — patience during first attempts pays off.
Optimize flask allocation per boss. Hard-hitting bosses demand more healing flasks, while spell-heavy builds should prioritize FP flasks for sustained damage.
Customize your Physick/Wondrous Elixir for each fight. Vigor-boosting tears combined with damage-negation tears cover offense and defense simultaneously.
Attune a diverse spell loadout. Ranged projectiles for approach, AoE for crowds, buffs for bosses, and utility spells for exploration cover all scenarios.
Upgrade a secondary weapon to +9/+24 minimum. Status-infused backup weapons (Bleed, Frost, Poison) or different movesets give options against resistant bosses.
Aim for poise breakpoints if your build supports it. 51+ poise in Elden Ring, 40+ in DS3, or max poise in DS1 lets you trade through enemy attacks.
Equip the strongest defensive talisman available. Dragoncrest Greatshield / Steel Protection +3 provides 20% physical damage reduction — a massive effective HP boost.
Test your build against optional superbosses before the final encounter. If you can handle the hardest optional boss, the final boss is manageable.
Record your damage numbers before and after optimization. Understanding the difference between 60% optimization and 95% optimization helps prioritize remaining upgrades.

builds.name: Colossal Knight
builds.description:
Colossal Knight is a pure strength build with the greatsword or giant-crusher. Designed around high Strength 80, Vigor 60, Endurance 40, this build achieves a easy difficulty level that welcomes newcomers while satisfying veterans. The build fully utilizes DLC content, incorporating endgame weapons, spells, and talismans that significantly elevate its performance.

In PvE, Colossal Knight handles every challenge with confidence. Boss fights become a dance of positioning and timing as you leverage the Greatsword's unique properties. Regular enemies and area traversal feel smooth thanks to the balanced stat investment — you have enough damage to clear trash efficiently and enough Vigor to survive surprises. The build prioritizes sustainable damage output through its primary stat while maintaining the defensive stats needed to learn new boss patterns without frustration.

The core strength of Colossal Knight is its accessibility and consistent performance. Key items like Greatsword are obtained early in the game, allowing the build to come online at a reasonable point. The primary weakness is occasional reliance on specific items or buffs — maintaining uptime requires attention. Players should experiment with different weapons of the same class to find their preferred moveset.

Designed with newer players in mind, Colossal Knight is straightforward to assemble and play effectively from the start. Item locations are accessible early, and the playstyle doesn't demand complex input sequences or frame-perfect timing. Veterans will appreciate the raw efficiency — this build deletes content without requiring excessive setup or consumable management. Whether this is your first playthrough or your tenth, you'll find satisfaction in the consistent, reliable performance this build delivers across all content.

builds.name: Pyromancer
builds.description:
Pyromancer is an intelligence/faith hybrid using the prince of death's staff and golden order seal. Designed around high Intelligence 45, Faith 45, Vigor 40, this build achieves a moderate difficulty level that rewards game knowledge and mechanical skill. The build fully utilizes DLC content, incorporating endgame weapons, spells, and talismans that significantly elevate its performance.

In PvE, Pyromancer handles every challenge with confidence. Boss fights become a dance of positioning and timing as you leverage the Prince of Death's Staff's unique properties. Regular enemies and area traversal feel smooth thanks to the balanced stat investment — you have enough damage to clear trash efficiently and enough Vigor to survive surprises. The build prioritizes sustainable damage output through its primary stat while maintaining the defensive stats needed to learn new boss patterns without frustration.

The core strength of Pyromancer is its versatility and damage potential when optimized. Key items like Prince of Death's Staff are acquired through mid-game progression or specific questlines, allowing the build to come online at a reasonable point. The primary weakness is occasional reliance on specific items or buffs — maintaining uptime requires attention. Players should practice the core combos regularly to build muscle memory.

Pyromancer is ideal for players who have completed at least one playthrough and want to explore a different approach to combat. It rewards game knowledge — knowing where key items are, which bosses to tackle in order, and how to optimize your route makes a significant difference. While the core build functions with basic items, reaching its full potential requires exploring optional areas, completing specific NPC questlines, and understanding soft cap breakpoints for efficient leveling.
builds.descriptionVi: Build Intelligence/Faith hybrid vi Prince of Death's Staff v Golden Order Seal. Tip cn ton b sorcery v incantation vi sát thng lửa.

phases.name: Early Game
steps: Prioritize leveling Vigor/Vitality to comfortable levels before investing heavily in damage stats — survival comes first in the early game, aim for 20 Vigor before focusing on Intelligence.
Explore Limgrave, Weeping Peninsula, Stormhill thoroughly. Each cave, catacomb, and ruin contains valuable upgrade materials, spells, and consumables crucial for progression.
Talk to every NPC you encounter — many offer questlines that reward essential items like Prince of Death's Staff or key upgrade materials later. Never attack NPCs unless you know their drops.
Save Smithing Stones and upgrade materials for weapons you'll use long-term. Your starting Astrologer weapon is adequate while you rush toward Prince of Death's Staff.
Purchase a backup weapon from a merchant — having a Strike weapon for crystal/skeleton enemies and a Thrust weapon for armored foes covers all resistances.
Master your weapon's moveset in early areas. Practice spacing on basic soldiers, roll timing against large enemies, and learn which attacks have poise/hyper armor.
Summon NPC phantoms for tough early bosses if needed. Many games hide summon signs near boss fogs — the game expects you to use them.
Collect every flask upgrade item — Golden Seeds, Estus Shards, Sacred Tears. Each upgrade provides more value than several stat points for survival.
Revisit merchants after major story progression — they often stock new items, spells, or unlimited upgrade materials after key milestones.
Rush toward your build's defining weapon early. Run past enemies if necessary — the sooner you get Prince of Death's Staff, the sooner your build comes online.
Kill every optional boss and mini-boss you encounter. They drop unique weapons, talismans, and valuable souls/runes for early leveling.
Buy basic spells (Glintstone Pebble equivalent) from early vendors. Even weak spells are excellent for clearing trash packs and pulling enemies from safe range.
Keep Endurance/Stamina at comfortable levels (15-20 early). An extra swing or roll often means the difference between winning and dying.
Experiment with Weapon Arts / Skills early. The Pick Astrologer for high Int start determines your early game approach.
Check the Whetblade / Infusion item availability. Changing weapon affinity early lets you scale with your primary damage stat from the start.

phases.name: Mid Game
steps: Reach your weapon's stat requirements to unlock its full potential. Intelligence should be your primary focus, with secondary investment in supporting stats.
Complete NPC questlines tied to your build. Many reward Prince of Death's Staff, powerful talismans, or unique spells. Check in with quest givers after each major boss.
Farm upgrade materials from specific mid-game enemies. Caelid and Altus Plateau have excellent farming spots for Chunks and upgrade materials.
Consider respeccing if your stats are suboptimal. Most games offer respec items (Larval Tear, Soul Vessel) — use them to fine-tune your Intelligence investment.
Equip talismans/rings that synergize with your damage type. Intelligence-boosting talismans (Scorpion Charms, Clutch Rings, Firstborn Rings) provide significant multipliers.
Explore optional areas before pushing main story progression. Mt. Gelmir and Nokron contain vital mid-game pickups for your build.
Join a covenant aligned with your playstyle. Many offer rewards like spell slots, faster casting, or damage buffs at rank milestones.
Invest in Mind/FP or Attunement if your build uses skills or spells. Running out of FP mid-fight is a common and preventable cause of death.
Find the best catalyst/seal/staff for your build. Courts Sorcerer Staff equivalents provide S-tier scaling for pure Intelligence builds.
Practice your core combat loop against mid-game enemies. Learn boss punish windows and optimal damage combos for your weapon class.
Collect respec items and keep them for emergencies. Having 2-3 respecs available lets you experiment with different stat distributions.
Target 35-40 Vigor/Vitality by mid-game. Weapon upgrade level contributes more to damage than raw stats at this stage — invest in survival first.
Maintain medium roll (under 70% equip load) at minimum. Fast roll (under 30%) is ideal for lighter builds. Defense and poise protect more than fashion.
Use consumables matching boss weaknesses. Altus Plateau bosses are particularly vulnerable to specific damage types — prepare accordingly.
Stockpile crafting materials. Resins, spell buffs, and consumables for your damage type provide 15-30% DPS increases that scale with your upgrades.

steps: Push Intelligence to the soft cap for maximum damage scaling. The 80 soft cap provides the best returns for spell scaling weapons.
Max your primary weapon to the highest upgrade level. Every level at high stat investment provides significant AR increases — check for Somber/Regular upgrade paths.
Farm the best talismans/rings/gems from endgame areas. Mountaintops of the Giants and Crumbling Farum Azula contain S-tier upgrades that transform your build's power.
Complete the DLC content before the final boss. DLC areas contain some of the game's best weapons, talismans, and spells — including direct upgrades for Prince of Death's Staff.
Stack multiplicative damage bonuses. Intelligence Scorpion Charm, Clutch Ring, or covenant rings combined with skill damage talismans provide exponential returns.
Use Terra Magicus / Steady Chant / Magic-boosting physick before boss doors. Buffing before entering maximizes your burst damage windows.
Learn endgame boss patterns through repetition. Miquella's Haligtree and Realm of Shadow bosses have complex mix-ups — patience during first attempts pays off.
Optimize flask allocation per boss. Hard-hitting bosses demand more healing flasks, while spell-heavy builds should prioritize FP flasks for sustained damage.
Customize your Physick/Wondrous Elixir for each fight. Intelligence-boosting tears combined with damage-negation tears cover offense and defense simultaneously.
Attune a diverse spell loadout. Ranged projectiles for approach, AoE for crowds, buffs for bosses, and utility spells for exploration cover all scenarios.

The build prioritizes sustainable damage output through its primary stat while maintaining the defensive stats needed to learn new boss patterns without frustration.

The core strength of Lightning Zealot is its accessibility and consistent performance. Players should experiment with different weapons of the same class to find their preferred moveset.

Designed with newer players in mind, Lightning Zealot is straightforward to assemble and play effectively from the start. Item locations are accessible early, and the playstyle doesn't demand complex input sequences or frame-perfect timing. Veterans will appreciate the raw efficiency — this build deletes content without requiring excessive setup or consumable management. Whether this is your first playthrough or your tenth, you'll find satisfaction in the consistent, reliable performance this build delivers across all content.

Regular enemies and area traversal feel smooth thanks to the balanced stat investment — you have enough damage to clear trash efficiently and enough Vigor to survive surprises. The build prioritizes sustainable damage output through its primary stat while maintaining the defensive stats needed to learn new boss patterns without frustration.

The core strength of Death's Poker is its versatility and damage potential when optimized. Key items like Death's Poker are acquired through mid-game progression or specific questlines, allowing the build to come online at a reasonable point. The primary weakness is occasional reliance on specific items or buffs — maintaining uptime requires attention. Players should practice the core combos regularly to build muscle memory.

Death's Poker is ideal for players who have completed at least one playthrough and want to explore a different approach to combat. It rewards game knowledge — knowing where key items are, which bosses to tackle in order, and how to optimize your route makes a significant difference. While the core build functions with basic items, reaching its full potential requires exploring optional areas, completing specific NPC questlines, and understanding soft cap breakpoints for efficient leveling.

builds.name: Magma Wyrm Scalesword
builds.description:
Magma Wyrm Scalesword is a strength/faith build using the magma wyrm scalesword. Designed around high Vigor 55, Strength 55, Endurance 30, this build achieves a easy difficulty level that welcomes newcomers while satisfying veterans.

In PvE, Magma Wyrm Scalesword handles every challenge with confidence. Boss fights become a dance of positioning and timing as you leverage the Magma Wyrm Scalesword's unique properties. Regular enemies and area traversal feel smooth thanks to the balanced stat investment — you have enough damage to clear trash efficiently and enough Vigor to survive surprises. The build prioritizes sustainable damage output through its primary stat while maintaining the defensive stats needed to learn new boss patterns without frustration.

The core strength of Magma Wyrm Scalesword is its accessibility and consistent performance. Key items like Magma Wyrm Scalesword are obtained early in the game, allowing the build to come online at a reasonable point. The primary weakness is occasional reliance on specific items or buffs — maintaining uptime requires attention. Players should experiment with different weapons of the same class to find their preferred moveset.

Designed with newer players in mind, Magma Wyrm Scalesword is straightforward to assemble and play effectively from the start. Item locations are accessible early, and the playstyle doesn't demand complex input sequences or frame-perfect timing. Veterans will appreciate the raw efficiency — this build deletes content without requiring excessive setup or consumable management. Whether this is your first playthrough or your tenth, you'll find satisfaction in the consistent, reliable performance this build delivers across all content.

phases.name: Early Game
steps: Prioritize leveling Vigor/Vitality to comfortable levels before investing heavily in damage stats — survival comes first in the early game, aim for 20 Vigor before focusing on Vigor.
Explore Limgrave, Weeping Peninsula, Stormhill thoroughly. Each cave, catacomb, and ruin contains valuable upgrade materials, spells, and consumables crucial for progression.
Talk to every NPC you encounter — many offer questlines that reward essential items like Magma Wyrm Scalesword or key upgrade materials later. Never attack NPCs unless you know their drops.
Save Smithing Stones and upgrade materials for weapons you'll use long-term. Your starting Hero weapon is adequate while you rush toward Magma Wyrm Scalesword.
Purchase a backup weapon from a merchant — having a Strike weapon for crystal/skeleton enemies and a Thrust weapon for armored foes covers all resistances.
Master your weapon's moveset in early areas. Practice spacing on basic soldiers, roll timing against large enemies, and learn which attacks have poise/hyper armor.
Summon NPC phantoms for tough early bosses if needed. Many games hide summon signs near boss fogs — the game expects you to use them.
Collect every flask upgrade item — Golden Seeds, Estus Shards, Sacred Tears. Each upgrade provides more value than several stat points for survival.
Revisit merchants after major story progression — they often stock new items, spells, or unlimited upgrade materials after key milestones.
Rush toward your build's defining weapon early. Run past enemies if necessary — the sooner you get Magma Wyrm Scalesword, the sooner your build comes online.
Kill every optional boss and mini-boss you encounter. They drop unique weapons, talismans, and valuable souls/runes for early leveling.
Buy basic spells (Glintstone Pebble equivalent) from early vendors. Even weak spells are excellent for clearing trash packs and pulling enemies from safe range.
Keep Endurance/Stamina at comfortable levels (15-20 early). An extra swing or roll often means the difference between winning and dying.
Experiment with Weapon Arts / Skills early. The Pick Hero for high Strength determines your early game approach.
Check the Whetblade / Infusion item availability. Changing weapon affinity early lets you scale with your primary damage stat from the start.

phases.name: Mid Game
steps: Reach your weapon's stat requirements to unlock its full potential. Vigor should be your primary focus, with secondary investment in supporting stats.
Complete NPC questlines tied to your build. Many reward Magma Wyrm Scalesword, powerful talismans, or unique spells. Check in with quest givers after each major boss.
Farm upgrade materials from specific mid-game enemies. Caelid and Altus Plateau have excellent farming spots for Chunks and upgrade materials.
Consider respeccing if your stats are suboptimal. Most games offer respec items (Larval Tear, Soul Vessel) — use them to fine-tune your Vigor investment.
Equip talismans/rings that synergize with your damage type. Vigor-boosting talismans (Scorpion Charms, Clutch Rings, Firstborn Rings) provide significant multipliers.
Explore optional areas before pushing main story progression. Mt. Gelmir and Nokron contain vital mid-game pickups for your build.
Join a covenant aligned with your playstyle. Many offer rewards like spell slots, faster casting, or damage buffs at rank milestones.
Invest in Mind/FP or Attunement if your build uses skills or spells. Running out of FP mid-fight is a common and preventable cause of death.
Find the best catalyst/seal/staff for your build. Dragon Communion Seal and Prince of Death's Staff provide hybrid scaling.
Practice your core combat loop against mid-game enemies. Learn boss punish windows and optimal damage combos for your weapon class.
Collect respec items and keep them for emergencies. Having 2-3 respecs available lets you experiment with different stat distributions.
Target 35-40 Vigor/Vitality by mid-game. Weapon upgrade level contributes more to damage than raw stats at this stage — invest in survival first.
Maintain medium roll (under 70% equip load) at minimum. Fast roll (under 30%) is ideal for lighter builds. Defense and poise protect more than fashion.
Use consumables matching boss weaknesses. Altus Plateau bosses are particularly vulnerable to specific damage types — prepare accordingly.
Stockpile crafting materials. Resins, spell buffs, and consumables for your damage type provide 15-30% DPS increases that scale with your upgrades.

phases.name: Late Game
steps: Push Vigor to the soft cap for maximum damage scaling. 40 is the standard soft cap for survivability stats.
Max your primary weapon to the highest upgrade level. Every level at high stat investment provides significant AR increases — check for Somber/Regular upgrade paths.
Farm the best talismans/rings/gems from endgame areas. Mountaintops of the Giants and Crumbling Farum Azula contain S-tier upgrades that transform your build's power.
Clear optional endgame areas for their unique rewards. Hidden bosses drop some of the best items in the base game.
Stack multiplicative damage bonuses. Vigor Scorpion Charm, Clutch Ring, or covenant rings combined with skill damage talismans provide exponential returns.
Use Terra Magicus / Steady Chant / Magic-boosting physick before boss doors. Buffing before entering maximizes your burst damage windows.
Learn endgame boss patterns through repetition. Miquella's Haligtree and Realm of Shadow bosses have complex mix-ups — patience during first attempts pays off.
Optimize flask allocation per boss. Hard-hitting bosses demand more healing flasks, while spell-heavy builds should prioritize FP flasks for sustained damage.
Customize your Physick/Wondrous Elixir for each fight. Vigor-boosting tears combined with damage-negation tears cover offense and defense simultaneously.
Attune a diverse spell loadout. Ranged projectiles for approach, AoE for crowds, buffs for bosses, and utility spells for exploration cover all scenarios.
Upgrade a secondary weapon to +9/+24 minimum. Status-infused backup weapons (Bleed, Frost, Poison) or different movesets give options against resistant bosses.
Aim for poise breakpoints if your build supports it. 51+ poise in Elden Ring, 40+ in DS3, or max poise in DS1 lets you trade through enemy attacks.
Equip the strongest defensive talisman available. Dragoncrest Greatshield / Steel Protection +3 provides 20% physical damage reduction — a massive effective HP boost.
Test your build against optional superbosses before the final encounter. If you can handle the hardest optional boss, the final boss is manageable.
Record your damage numbers before and after optimization. Understanding the difference between 60% optimization and 95% optimization helps prioritize remaining upgrades.

This build is crafted for veteran players who understand the game's mechanics on a deep level. It demands precise knowledge of stat breakpoints, item locations, and combat timing. The payoff for mastery is immense — Parry King Dagger ranks among the most powerful setups when played optimally. Every aspect of the build, from the Dexterity 55, Vigor 50, Endurance 30 stat distribution to the Misericorde weapon choice, is optimized for a specific purpose. This is not a build to learn the game with but one to master it with.

builds.name: Beastial Claw
builds.description:
Beastial Claw is a beast-themed build using the beast claw weapon from the dlc combined with bestial incantations. Designed around high Vigor 50, Strength 40, Dexterity 40, this build achieves a moderate difficulty level that rewards game knowledge and mechanical skill. The build fully utilizes DLC content, incorporating endgame weapons, spells, and talismans that significantly elevate its performance.

In PvE, Beastial Claw handles every challenge with confidence. Boss fights become a dance of positioning and timing as you leverage the Beast Claw's unique properties. Regular enemies and area traversal feel smooth thanks to the balanced stat investment — you have enough damage to clear trash efficiently and enough Vigor to survive surprises. The build prioritizes sustainable damage output through its primary stat while maintaining the defensive stats needed to learn new boss patterns without frustration.

The core strength of Beastial Claw is its versatility and damage potential when optimized. Key items like Beast Claw are acquired through mid-game progression or specific questlines, allowing the build to come online at a reasonable point. The primary weakness is occasional reliance on specific items or buffs — maintaining uptime requires attention. Players should practice the core combos regularly to build muscle memory.

Beastial Claw is ideal for players who have completed at least one playthrough and want to explore a different approach to combat. It rewards game knowledge — knowing where key items are, which bosses to tackle in order, and how to optimize your route makes a significant difference. While the core build functions with basic items, reaching its full potential requires exploring optional areas, completing specific NPC questlines, and understanding soft cap breakpoints for efficient leveling.

phases.name: Early Game
steps: Prioritize leveling Vigor/Vitality to comfortable levels before investing heavily in damage stats — survival comes first in the early game, aim for 20 Vigor before focusing on Vigor.
Explore Limgrave, Weeping Peninsula, Stormhill thoroughly. Each cave, catacomb, and ruin contains valuable upgrade materials, spells, and consumables crucial for progression.
Talk to every NPC you encounter — many offer questlines that reward essential items like Beast Claw or key upgrade materials later. Never attack NPCs unless you know their drops.
Save Smithing Stones and upgrade materials for weapons you'll use long-term. Your starting Warrior weapon is adequate while you rush toward Beast Claw.
Purchase a backup weapon from a merchant — having a Strike weapon for crystal/skeleton enemies and a Thrust weapon for armored foes covers all resistances.
Master your weapon's moveset in early areas. Practice spacing on basic soldiers, roll timing against large enemies, and learn which attacks have poise/hyper armor.
Summon NPC phantoms for tough early bosses if needed. Many games hide summon signs near boss fogs — the game expects you to use them.
Collect every flask upgrade item — Golden Seeds, Estus Shards, Sacred Tears. Each upgrade provides more value than several stat points for survival.
Revisit merchants after major story progression — they often stock new items, spells, or unlimited upgrade materials after key milestones.
Rush toward your build's defining weapon early. Run past enemies if necessary — the sooner you get Beast Claw, the sooner your build comes online.
Kill every optional boss and mini-boss you encounter. They drop unique weapons, talismans, and valuable souls/runes for early leveling.
Buy basic spells (Glintstone Pebble equivalent) from early vendors. Even weak spells are excellent for clearing trash packs and pulling enemies from safe range.
Keep Endurance/Stamina at comfortable levels (15-20 early). An extra swing or roll often means the difference between winning and dying.
Experiment with Weapon Arts / Skills early. The Pick Warrior for balanced stats determines your early game approach.
Check the Whetblade / Infusion item availability. Changing weapon affinity early lets you scale with your primary damage stat from the start.

phases.name: Mid Game
steps: Reach your weapon's stat requirements to unlock its full potential. Vigor should be your primary focus, with secondary investment in supporting stats.
Complete NPC questlines tied to your build. Many reward Beast Claw, powerful talismans, or unique spells. Check in with quest givers after each major boss.
Farm upgrade materials from specific mid-game enemies. Caelid and Altus Plateau have excellent farming spots for Chunks and upgrade materials.
Consider respeccing if your stats are suboptimal. Most games offer respec items (Larval Tear, Soul Vessel) — use them to fine-tune your Vigor investment.
Equip talismans/rings that synergize with your damage type. Vigor-boosting talismans (Scorpion Charms, Clutch Rings, Firstborn Rings) provide significant multipliers.
Explore optional areas before pushing main story progression. Mt. Gelmir and Nokron contain vital mid-game pickups for your build.
Join a covenant aligned with your playstyle. Many offer rewards like spell slots, faster casting, or damage buffs at rank milestones.
Invest in Mind/FP or Attunement if your build uses skills or spells. Running out of FP mid-fight is a common and preventable cause of death.
Find the best catalyst/seal/staff for your build. Dragon Communion Seal and Prince of Death's Staff provide hybrid scaling.
Practice your core combat loop against mid-game enemies. Learn boss punish windows and optimal damage combos for your weapon class.
Collect respec items and keep them for emergencies. Having 2-3 respecs available lets you experiment with different stat distributions.
Target 35-40 Vigor/Vitality by mid-game. Weapon upgrade level contributes more to damage than raw stats at this stage — invest in survival first.
Maintain medium roll (under 70% equip load) at minimum. Fast roll (under 30%) is ideal for lighter builds. Defense and poise protect more than fashion.
Use consumables matching boss weaknesses. Altus Plateau bosses are particularly vulnerable to specific damage types — prepare accordingly.
Stockpile crafting materials. Resins, spell buffs, and consumables for your damage type provide 15-30% DPS increases that scale with your upgrades.

phases.name: Late Game
steps: Push Vigor to the soft cap for maximum damage scaling. 40 is the standard soft cap for survivability stats.
Max your primary weapon to the highest upgrade level. Every level at high stat investment provides significant AR increases — check for Somber/Regular upgrade paths.
Farm the best talismans/rings/gems from endgame areas. Mountaintops of the Giants and Crumbling Farum Azula contain S-tier upgrades that transform your build's power.
Complete the DLC content before the final boss. DLC areas contain some of the game's best weapons, talismans, and spells — including direct upgrades for Beast Claw.
Stack multiplicative damage bonuses. Vigor Scorpion Charm, Clutch Ring, or covenant rings combined with skill damage talismans provide exponential returns.
Use Terra Magicus / Steady Chant / Magic-boosting physick before boss doors. Buffing before entering maximizes your burst damage windows.
Learn endgame boss patterns through repetition. Miquella's Haligtree and Realm of Shadow bosses have complex mix-ups — patience during first attempts pays off.
Optimize flask allocation per boss. Hard-hitting bosses demand more healing flasks, while spell-heavy builds should prioritize FP flasks for sustained damage.
Customize your Physick/Wondrous Elixir for each fight. Vigor-boosting tears combined with damage-negation tears cover offense and defense simultaneously.
Attune a diverse spell loadout. Ranged projectiles for approach, AoE for crowds, buffs for bosses, and utility spells for exploration cover all scenarios.
Upgrade a secondary weapon to +9/+24 minimum. Status-infused backup weapons (Bleed, Frost, Poison) or different movesets give options against resistant bosses.
Aim for poise breakpoints if your build supports it. 51+ poise in Elden Ring, 40+ in DS3, or max poise in DS1 lets you trade through enemy attacks.
Equip the strongest defensive talisman available. Dragoncrest Greatshield / Steel Protection +3 provides 20% physical damage reduction — a massive effective HP boost.
Test your build against optional superbosses before the final encounter. If you can handle the hardest optional boss, the final boss is manageable.
Record your damage numbers before and after optimization. Understanding the difference between 60% optimization and 95% optimization helps prioritize remaining upgrades.

The build prioritizes sustainable damage output through its primary stat while maintaining the defensive stats needed to learn new boss patterns without frustration.

The core strength of Pure Faith Caster is its versatility and damage potential when optimized. Punch Out is an only fist weapons. Designed around high Strength 60, Vigor 55, Endurance 40, this build achieves a moderate difficulty level that rewards game knowledge and mechanical skill. While you won't top damage charts, you'll have an unforgettable experience trolling invaders, surprising co-op partners, and enjoying the game from a completely different perspective. steps: Push Vigor to the soft cap for maximum damage scaling. 40 is the standard soft cap for survivability stats.
Max your primary weapon to the highest upgrade level. Every level at high stat investment provides significant AR increases — check for Somber/Regular upgrade paths.
Farm the best talismans/rings/gems from endgame areas. Mountaintops of the Giants and Crumbling Farum Azula contain S-tier upgrades that transform your build's power.
Clear optional endgame areas for their unique rewards. Hidden bosses drop some of the best items in the base game.
Stack multiplicative damage bonuses. Vigor Scorpion Charm, Clutch Ring, or covenant rings combined with skill damage talismans provide exponential returns.
Use Terra Magicus / Steady Chant / Magic-boosting physick before boss doors. Buffing before entering maximizes your burst damage windows.
Learn endgame boss patterns through repetition. Miquella's Haligtree and Realm of Shadow bosses have complex mix-ups — patience during first attempts pays off.
Optimize flask allocation per boss. Hard-hitting bosses demand more healing flasks, while spell-heavy builds should prioritize FP flasks for sustained damage.
Customize your Physick/Wondrous Elixir for each fight. Vigor-boosting tears combined with damage-negation tears cover offense and defense simultaneously.
Attune a diverse spell loadout. Ranged projectiles for approach, AoE for crowds, buffs for bosses, and utility spells for exploration cover all scenarios.
Upgrade a secondary weapon to +9/+24 minimum. Status-infused backup weapons (Bleed, Frost, Poison) or different movesets give options against resistant bosses.
Aim for poise breakpoints if your build supports it. 51+ poise in Elden Ring, 40+ in DS3, or max poise in DS1 lets you trade through enemy attacks.
Equip the strongest defensive talisman available. Dragoncrest Greatshield / Steel Protection +3 provides 20% physical damage reduction — a massive effective HP boost.
Test your build against optional superbosses before the final encounter. If you can handle the hardest optional boss, the final boss is manageable.
Record your damage numbers before and after optimization. Understanding the difference between 60% optimization and 95% optimization helps prioritize remaining upgrades.

tips: Torches have low damage — this is a challenge run, not an efficient build
St. Trina's Torch can put enemies to sleep for free critical hits
Ghostflame Torch is actually decent against deathbirds and undead
The Beast-Repellent Torch keeps beasts at bay — useful for Caelid
You can equip a torch in each hand for dual-wield torch action (still bad but stylish)
Meme builds like Torch Hollow are about having fun. Don't worry about optimization — enjoy the unique playstyle and surprise factor.
Stat soft caps in Elden Ring: Vigor 40/60, Endurance 50, Str/Dex 55, Int/Fth/Arc 50/80. Know these for efficient leveling of Torch Hollow.
Jump attacks are king in Elden Ring — they deal massive stance damage and are safe against most attacks. Standard Torch users should abuse jumping R2s.
Spirit Ash summons can completely change a boss fight. Mimic Tear is the best general-purpose option for Torch Hollow.
Always carry a Strike weapon for crystal enemies and a Pierce weapon for heavily armored foes — Standard Torch may not handle all resistances.
The Wondrous Physick can be customized for each boss. Swap tears based on the fight for maximum advantage with Torch Hollow.
Guard counters (block + R2) are incredibly strong. They deal high stance damage and can break most enemies when using heavy weapons.
